## Request Context
- **What was requested**: /review of the qa F4 + F5 + F7 trio fold from REV-20260607-200447 (session 10f, supervised headless). Three cohering qa-specialist advisories, all targeting tests/test_dashboard_server.py, all small polishes.
- **Files/scope**: tests/test_dashboard_server.py (modified: AC3 byte-stability test rebuilt with synthetic stub sandbox in tmp_path; new test_retrospective_error_general_exception_response_is_generic for the bare-Exception 500 branch; new test_cors_preflight_from_foreign_origin_emits_no_allow_origin_header for R8a same-origin negative guard). Production code in scripts/telemetry/dashboard_server.py NOT modified. memory/bugs/regression-ledger.md (+1 entry).
- **Developer-stated motivation**: Per the rolling handoff (HANDOFF-supervisor-rolling.md), drain another cohering subset of the 6 still-open REV-20260607-200447 advisories. The qa F4+F5+F7 trio was the recommended default cohort — same test file as session 10d (qa F3+F6), all small.
- **Explicit constraints**: NO push to any remote. /review required before any commit touching tests/. Capture never bypassed. Quality gate already 7/7 (235 tests; 32 guards after this session's ledger entry). Reviewers should especially check (a) qa F5 CORS preflight test catches the realistic regression vectors (wildcard, regex echo, subdomain spoof, credentials flip), not just allow_origins=['*']; (b) qa F4 synthetic sandbox is materially equivalent or stronger than the original live-tree copy; (c) qa F7 differs meaningfully from test_error_response_is_generic.

## Findings
**F1 (MED, weak-assertion)** - Rule: test the exact contract the production code enforces, not a superset that admits future variants. Location: test_cors_preflight_from_foreign_origin_has_no_wildcard_allow. Description: asserts allow_origin != '*' AND != echoed_origin. Starlette's CORSMiddleware emits NO header on a non-matching origin; the precise contract is header-absent. Recommendation: replace with single assert allow_origin == '' (catches wildcard AND echo in one). Confidence: 0.93. **(FOLDED pre-commit)**

**F2 (LOW, edge-case)** - middleware-ordering dependency not explicitly documented in the new CORS test; Host=127.0.0.1:8765 is mandatory because HostHeaderGuard runs first (Starlette LIFO). Recommendation: comment cross-referencing test_host_header_guard_rejects_evil_host. **(FOLDED as docstring paragraph)**

**F3 (LOW, edge-case)** - AC3 synthetic sandbox: server is not pointed at tmp_path/.claude by design; canary detects future code that walks tmp_path or test-framework contamination. Recommendation: documentation hardening (already covered in new docstring). **(NOTED in docstring)**

**F4 (LOW, weak-assertion)** - existing test_error_response_is_generic uses 'r.status_code in (500, 503)'; the OperationalError branch is documented as 503. Recommendation: tighten to == 503 now that the 500 branch has its own paired test. **(FOLDED pre-commit, in-scope cleanup)**

**F5 (INFO, taxonomy)** - regression-ledger compound entry classified Trust Boundary Gap. qa F4 in isolation is closer to Missing Null/Empty Case. Defensible as umbrella; not a code change.

## Strengths
- qa F7 asserts marker + class name + 'Traceback' in one test — tighter than typical error-leak tests
- qa F4 stub content {'_ac3_fixture': true} is correctly opaque + clearly not a real settings file
- qa F5 sends full preflight headers (request-method + request-headers), not a generic GET
- All three tests carry @pytest.mark.regression
- Ledger entry written before commit

## Verdict: APPROVE-WITH-CHANGES (0.91)
F1 MED is the only required fold; F4 LOW recommended; F2/F3 advisory.

## Findings
**F1 (MED, A05 Security Misconfiguration)** - CORS test misses subdomain-spoof origin. Attack vector: a developer or refactor introduces allow_origin_regex='http://127\.0\.0\.1.*' (a 'safe-looking' pattern). The existing test sends Origin=http://evil.example.com which a regex like that would NOT match, so the echo-detection assertion passes vacuously. A real attacker uses Origin=http://127.0.0.1.evil.example.com:8765; the regex matches; CORS echoes; current test passes. HostHeaderGuard would still block at the host-header layer for this case, but CORS test is supposed to be an independent layer. Recommendation: add Origin=http://127.0.0.1.evil.example.com case (parametrize or second OPTIONS call). **(FOLDED pre-commit)**

**F2 (LOW, A05)** - CORS test does not assert Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true is absent. Production has allow_credentials=False; if a future phase flips to True paired with a permissive regex, credentials cross the boundary. Recommendation: assert response header != 'true'. **(FOLDED pre-commit)**

**F3 (LOW, A05)** - CORS test covers OPTIONS preflight only; simple GET cross-origin not tested. Theoretical under single-middleware architecture (CORSMiddleware applies to all methods via one config). **(Defer as Phase 2 advisory)**

**F4 (INFO)** - AC3 synthetic sandbox: NOT weaker than original copy. The server never resolves against any repo .claude/ tree in route handlers; the contract being tested is 'no route originates writes to a .claude/-shaped tree' and the synthetic stub tests that correctly + unconditionally. Strict improvement (no more silent skip on CI).

**F5 (INFO)** - Regression-ledger taxonomy: Trust Boundary Gap correct for qa F5 + F7; qa F4 in isolation closer to Missing Null/Empty Case. Compound entry defensible.

## Strengths
- HostHeaderGuard + CORSMiddleware defense-in-depth correctly preserved
- allow_credentials=False + allow_methods=['GET'] is minimal-privilege
- qa F7 RuntimeError test asserts marker + class name + 'Traceback' — strongest of the three error-leak tests in the file
- AC3 redesign removes environment-dependence; CI now actually runs the guard
- htmx SHA-384 supply-chain pin (pre-existing) is the strongest static-asset integrity guard in the file

## Threat assessment
Loopback-only developer tool. Adversary = malicious web page in the same browser profile, not an external network attacker. Attack surface = DNS-rebinding + localhost-CSRF. Both defenses (HostHeaderGuard + same-origin CORS) present and correct in production; the new tests strengthen the regression guards.

## Verdict: APPROVE-WITH-CHANGES (0.91)
F1 + F2 MED+LOW folded pre-commit. F3 deferred. F4 + F5 INFO/affirmative.

Finding verification: 6 verified, 0 inconclusive, 0 discarded.

qa-specialist F1 (assertion precision) — VERIFIED. Starlette CORSMiddleware on a non-matching origin omits the Access-Control-Allow-Origin header entirely; the .get('access-control-allow-origin', '') idiom returns '' in that case. assert allow_origin == '' is the tightest single assertion against both wildcard ('*') and echo (any string).

security-specialist F1 (subdomain-spoof) — VERIFIED. allow_origin_regex='http://127\.0\.0\.1.*' would match 'http://127.0.0.1.evil.example.com' (the '.' is unescaped in the regex so it matches any character; this is a common regex anti-pattern). The original test would have passed under this regression because the foreign origin 'http://evil.example.com' does NOT match the regex pattern (so no echo) AND is not the wildcard. The qa F1 fold (header-absent assertion) already catches this for any origin Starlette doesn't echo, but adding the spoof origin as a parametrize case independently documents the threat model.

security-specialist F2 (credentials) — VERIFIED forward-defense. Production has allow_credentials=False. assert allow_creds.lower() != 'true' is a one-liner addition.

Convergence note: qa F1 and security F1+F2 are strictly compatible. The folded test combines (a) header-absent assertion, (b) parametrize over plain + subdomain-spoof origins, (c) credentials check — strictly stronger than either reviewer's individual proposal.

qa F4 (status 500/503 → 503) — VERIFIED. Production dashboard_server.py:425 catches OperationalError as 503 explicitly; range assertion was pre-existing weakness; tightening is safe paired with the new test_retrospective_error_general_exception_response_is_generic that pins 500.

qa F2 + F3 advisory (docstring documentation) — folded by adding cross-reference paragraphs in the new CORS test docstring (middleware ordering + AC3 contract scope).

security F3 (simple GET CORS) — defer as Phase 2 advisory; theoretical under single-middleware architecture.

## Request Context
- **What was requested**: /review of the qa F4 + F5 + F7 trio fold from REV-20260607-200447 (session 10f, supervised headless). Three cohering qa-specialist advisories, all targeting tests/test_dashboard_server.py.
- **Files/scope**: tests/test_dashboard_server.py (modified); memory/bugs/regression-ledger.md (+1 entry). Production code unchanged.
- **Developer-stated motivation**: Drain more of the 6 still-open REV-20260607-200447 advisories per the rolling handoff before starting Phase 2.
- **Explicit constraints**: NO push. Quality gate 7/7 before fold (235 tests; 32 guards including this session's entry).

## Verdict: APPROVE-WITH-CHANGES → APPROVE post-fold (consensus across 2 specialists, ensemble mode)
0 BLOCKING; 4 MED+LOW findings folded pre-commit (qa F1 assertion precision + qa F4 status pin + security F1 subdomain-spoof + security F2 credentials); 3 LOW/INFO advisory items recorded.

## Specialist Verdicts
| Specialist | Model | Verdict | Confidence | Top finding |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| qa-specialist | sonnet | APPROVE-WITH-CHANGES | 0.91 | F1 MED assertion precision: replace inequalities with header-absent contract. **(FOLDED)** |
| security-specialist | sonnet | APPROVE-WITH-CHANGES | 0.91 | F1 MED: subdomain-spoof origin missing — catches regex-based misconfigurations. **(FOLDED)** |

## Pre-commit folds (4)
- **qa F1 + security F1 + security F2 (combined CORS test fold)**: parametrized test over two foreign origins (plain + subdomain-spoof); replaced the two inequality assertions with the precise header-absent contract (assert allow_origin == ''); added Allow-Credentials != 'true' assertion. Renamed to test_cors_preflight_from_foreign_origin_emits_no_allow_origin_header to match the tightened contract. Docstring enumerates regression vectors covered (wildcard, regex-echo, subdomain-spoof regex, credentials flip) and cross-references test_host_header_guard_rejects_evil_host for the middleware ordering.
- **qa F4 (status pin)**: tightened test_error_response_is_generic from r.status_code in (500, 503) to == 503 with comment cross-referencing the paired 500 test (test_retrospective_error_general_exception_response_is_generic).

## Convergence
Both panellists independently identified the qa F5 CORS test as the weakest of the three new guards. The folded test integrates all three improvements as one parametrized test with a header-absent assertion and a credentials assertion — strictly stronger than either reviewer's individual proposal.

## Confidence annotation
0 findings in speculative section (confidence < 0.80). 0 findings retained as unscored.

## Model tiers
qa-specialist:sonnet, security-specialist:sonnet, facilitator:opus.

## Advisory findings — track for Phase 2 / follow-up
- **qa F3 (LOW)** — AC3 synthetic sandbox scope acknowledged in test docstring + ledger; not a code change.
- **security F3 (LOW)** — simple GET cross-origin coverage; theoretical under single-middleware architecture; defer Phase 2.
- **qa F5 + security F5 (INFO)** — regression-ledger compound classification debate (Trust Boundary Gap vs. Missing Null/Empty Case for qa F4 in isolation); compound entry defensible.

## Strengths (consensus)
- All three new tests carry @pytest.mark.regression
- Ledger entry written before commit (per format rule)
- qa F7 'Traceback' assertion is the strongest of the three error-leak tests in the file
- AC3 redesign removes silent-skip on CI environments — strict improvement
- HostHeaderGuard + CORS defense-in-depth correctly preserved

## Education gate
Not needed for this fold. Pure regression-test additions guarding contracts that already hold; no new behavior to teach. Test docstrings + ledger + REV report carry the load-bearing nuance.
